title: Priority-window coalescer for conversational bundling to optimize streaming completions
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Streaming chat workloads show unpredictable P95 spikes caused by small, straggler messages and aggressive KV cache pressure when many mid-length conversations are active. Current microbatching groups by arrival time and token budget only, which leads to frequent GPU memory churn and suboptimal KV residency for conversational prefixes. Goals: 1) Reduce tail latency while preserving or improving throughput and token-level cost. 2) Reduce KV cache evictions of hot conversational prefixes. 3) Maintain real-time streaming semantics for foreground interactive sessions. Proposed approach: Implement a Priority-window coalescer (PWC) that forms bundles based on a short, sliding priority window instead of fixed time buckets. Each request is scored by a lightweight affinity tuple (priority, estimated remaining tokens, kv-hotness score). The PWC asynchronously maintains soft watermarks for GPU memory and KV occupancy. Within the sliding window, the coordinator attempts to coalesce requests that maximize aggregate affinity while respecting a deadline budget per request to avoid noticeable streaming stalls. The system supports polite preemption: if a high-priority interactive request arrives, it can preempt pending bundles up to a configurable fraction, and partially-filled GPU slabs are resequenced with minimal copying using pointer swaps and compacted KV descriptors.
acceptance_criteria: Tail latency (P95) for streaming completions reduced by >= 15% on the standard chat benchmark compared to baseline microbatcher
KV cache hot-prefix eviction rate decreased by >= 20% under the 10k-conversation mixed workload
Throughput (tokens/sec) degradation <= 5% compared to baseline when under steady load
No user-visible increase in streaming latency for foreground interactive sessions (per-route SLOs preserved)
Automated integration tests for deadline preemption and KV descriptor compacting added to CI
implementation_plan: Design PWC scoring function: implement priority, remaining_tokens estimator and kv-hotness probe (week 1)
Add sliding-window queue and lightweight scheduler to runtime request ingress path (week 2)
Implement soft watermark tracker for GPU memory and KV occupancy with backpressure hooks (week 2-3)
Add preemption and pointer-swap compaction in slab allocator to avoid memcpy on resequence (week 3)
Create simulation harness and run mixed-workload experiments to tune window size and deadline budgets (week 3-4)
Ship behind feature flag, run canary on dedicated pool, collect telemetry and iterate (week 5)
Docs + runbook + rollout playbook for console controls (week 6)
design_decisions: Use a sliding window instead of fixed time buckets to better capture bursty arrivals and reduce sensitivity to clock alignment
Score combines static customer priority, a running estimate of remaining tokens (based on prefix length and model average), and a kv-hotness probe that checks recent prefix hits
Prefer pointer-swap and descriptor compaction over memcpy for resequencing to reduce GPU memcpy overhead on large slabs
Expose two knobs in console: window_ms and deadline_fraction to allow SREs to tune for latency vs. cost on a per-customer basis
tradeoffs: Sliding window increases scheduler complexity and requires more bookkeeping per request, which slightly raises CPU overhead on the ingress path
Aggressive coalescing can increase per-request queuing time; mitigated by deadline budgets and preemption rules
Pointer-swap compaction reduces memcpy cost but increases allocator complexity and a small risk of fragmentation if not compacted periodically
KV-hotness probing adds extra KV-metadata lookups which may slightly increase request admission latency; we cache probes for a short TTL
risks_mitigation: Risk: scheduler bug could deadlock bundles. Mitigation: add watchdog that drains window after a max_wait_ms and falls back to baseline microbatcher
Risk: pointer-swap compaction corrupts descriptor under concurrent access. Mitigation: use atomic descriptor state transitions and add stress tests in CI
Risk: misconfigured knobs could cause regressions for low-tier customers. Mitigation: default conservative settings and gradual rollout with metric gates
Risk: KV probe amplification under heavy load. Mitigation: probe sampling and TTL caching to bound metadata queries

2026-03-05 - Marcus: Implemented sliding-window queue prototype and added basic scoring. Local microbench shows similar throughput and 6% P95 improvement on synthetic chat workload.

2026-03-07 - QA: Found edge case where preemption left tiny 32-byte fragments in slab allocator leading to fragmentation over time. Marcus added a periodic compaction pass to free fragments > 1MB total.
2026-03-08 - Performance: Simulation run with 10k-conversation trace shows KV hot-prefix eviction reduced by 12% with window_ms=12. Need further tuning to hit 20% target.
2026-03-09 - Marcus: Added KV-hotness probe caching (TTL=1s) and reduced probe sampling rate to 10% for low priority. This reduced metadata load in the sim by ~40%.
2026-03-10 - PR opened: runtime#1987. Core changes: sliding window scheduler, soft-watermark tracker, pointer-swap compaction. Still flagged experimental and behind flag.

2026-03-12 - Canary started on dedicated pool with feature flag enabled for 5% of traffic. Early telemetry: P95 down 18% on chat-variant A; KV eviction -21%; throughput steady. No errors in allocator logs so far. Next: expand to 20% if no regressions.
